Issued at 146 PM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Gourd-geous weather may not be in the cards for South Florida this 
Halloween as the forecast has trended wetter over the past 24 hours. 
There is no trick (or treat) here, as we will delve into all of the 
forecast specifics later in this discussion. But for now, the main 
takeaway is that rain chances have taken an upward trajectory for 
Saturday afternoon and evening, now in the 50-70% range with 
forecast temperatures in the upper 70s to low 80s forecast across 
the region during the same timeframe. Before we get too far ahead, 
let's rewind back to the beginning of the extended period and take a 
closer look at the end of the ongoing work week. 

While zonal mid-level flow will prevail across much of the 
southeastern United States Thursday night into Friday morning, the 
axis of a developing mid-level ridge across the southern Gulf will 
slide eastward during the second half of the week, resulting in 
increasing geopotential heights, 500mb temperatures above the 75-
90th percentile, and a reduction in 500mb wind speeds out of the 
northwest. The plume of deeper atmospheric moisture previously in 
place will gradually wane across the region with precipitable water 
values still slightly above average compared to climo, but remaining 
in the 60-70th percentile through Friday afternoon. Surface winds 
are forecast to remain out of a northeasterly direction across the 
region as the background flow regime is dominated by an expansive 
ridge of surface high pressure situated across the southeastern 
United States. The onshore breeze will result in a temperature 
gradient from east to west across the region, with forecasted high 
temperatures in the low to mid 80s along the east coast on Friday 
and temperatures in the upper 80s to near 90 across southwestern 
Florida.

The axis of mid-level ridging is forecast to slide across South 
Florida during the day on Saturday, however the enhancement of a 
pressure gradient between the aforementioned surface ridging across 
the southeastern United States and western Atlantic waters as well 
as an area of developing low pressure in the Gulf may result in an 
enhancement of winds across the northern half of South Florida 
during this time period. Moisture will pool out ahead of the feature 
which will act to increase rain chances across the region on 
Saturday afternoon as previously advertised above. Warm 500mb 
temperatures and ridging aloft will keep convection fairly benign in 
nature through the first half of the weekend. Mid-level ridging 
across our region is then forecast to erode Saturday night into 
Sunday morning as a lobe of mid-level vorticity slides eastward 
across the southeastern United States in tandem with a developing 
surface low and frontal boundary in the Gulf. Ample warm air and 
moisture advection is forecast to occur across the Florida Peninsula 
with the best atmospheric dynamics and ascent residing over the 
northern half of the Florida Peninsula. Ensemble and deterministic 
guidance has been both 1) more progressive with the mid-level 
vorticity over the past 24 hours and 2) more amplified with the mid-
level forcing in closer proximity to South Florida. A cooling of 
500mb temperatures to below average values (25th to 50th 
percentile), 500-700mb lapse rates steeping to 6.0 to 6.5 C/km, and 
a southerly component to surface winds could focus a higher chance 
of convection (including thunderstorms) across inland South Florida, 
Lake Okeechobee locales, and Palm Beach & Broward counties on Sunday 
afternoon and evening as activity is forecast to favor these 
regions. While we remain outside of the time horizon of reliable 
mesoscale models, the proximity of dynamics to the region, moisture 
advection, and instability could support the threat of an isolated 
strong to marginally severe storm, especially along any mesoscale 
boundary interactions. Stay tuned as more reliable model guidance 
comes in and we get a more complete picture on atmospheric dynamics. 

Beyond that, the amplified southern stream across the southeastern 
United States may briefly advect drier air on the westward side of 
the departing surface low that is forecast to transit just offshore 
of the southeastern United States early next week. This may result 
in lower rain chances on Tuesday and Wednesday as a lobe of mid-
level ridging briefly established across the region before more mid-
level vorticity knocks on our doorstep. All in all, it does not 
appear that South Florida will branch out into fall anytime soon as 
no strong cold fronts are on the immediate horizon.
